current_value: A burrowing starfish that churns the sand bed and feeds on worms, copepods, and small benthic invertebrates living in it. Demands a deep (7 cm+), well-established sand bed and roughly 280 L per specimen; once it exhausts the sand's food supply it quietly starves, so it suits mature systems only.

current_value: The most common fish disease — caused by Ichthyophthirius multifiliis, appearing as small white spots like salt grains. Highly contagious but treatable with temperature increase and medication.
proposed_value: Freshwater white-spot disease caused by Ichthyophthirius multifiliis. Diagnosis requires a wet mount; gill-only infections may show no spots. Treatment is not universal: formalin or copper are veterinary-listed options, but copper is toxic to invertebrates and plants and disrupts biofilters, formalin requires vigorous aeration, and repeated treatment/product guidance is required. Heat alone is not a substitute; seek specialist/product guidance and do not use a dose from this page.
